text: Membership is precisely the multiplicative valuation bound v(z)≤exp(−a). This agrees with the [valuation-ring convention](https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/00I8) and remains correct at zero and negative indices. The source-present zero-step and one-step identities fix the sign; the additive comparison explicitly excludes zero because ord(0) is totalized. No global function-field or finite-residue-field assumption is needed for this local identity. [Lean source](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/93d1fe508e122e53ce5538a8a3994c290753f127/TauCeti/FieldTheory/FunctionField/Place/Filtration.lean#L106).

The existing one-index formula identifies value below one, fixing the filtration sign and retaining zero.
The actual additive comparison explicitly requires the element to be nonzero.

An integral u congruent to one at filtration level a retains that congruence under every natural power. The published induction uses u(uⁿ−1)+(u−1), so integrality supplies the necessary level-zero multiplier. Its n=0 branch is the actual zero difference. This is the usual [valuation-ideal congruence](https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/00I8), valid also at negative levels; neither u≠0 nor a>0 is silently required. [Lean source](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/93d1fe508e122e53ce5538a8a3994c290753f127/TauCeti/FieldTheory/FunctionField/Place/Filtration.lean#L193).

The map evaluates z by multiplying by s in the function field and then taking its actual residue class. The equality exposes that computation, the local scaling-and-reduction map behind [Stichtenoth Lemma1.4.8](https://link.springer.com/chapter/10.1007/978-3-540-76878-4_1). The definition permits s=0,a=0 and correctly becomes zero. Source-present kernel and surjectivity theorems retain s≠0; this defining equation does not incorrectly claim those properties in the degenerate case. For nonzero scaling, the actual residue vanishes exactly on the next step; this guard is not omitted from the test.
The source constructs a preimage by lifting a residue and dividing by the nonzero scaling element.

The carrier is the families of elements of F that are integral outside a finite set of places, exactly the convention in [Stichtenoth Definition1.5.2](https://link.springer.com/chapter/10.1007/978-3-540-76878-4_1). Zero and scalar closure use the actual valuation and its triviality on k. Published finite-exception, valuation-ring and single-place formulas verify this carrier. The construction also makes sense for arbitrary field extensions; it asserts neither completed local entries nor finite dimension. [Lean source](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/93d1fe508e122e53ce5538a8a3994c290753f127/TauCeti/FieldTheory/FunctionField/Repartition/Basic.lean#L115).
The source identifies cofinite integrality with finiteness of the actual nonintegral exceptional set.
The source identifies the cofinite valuation bound with membership in each actual valuation ring.
The actual single-place repartition has its prescribed entry at the selected place.

This unfolds repartition membership as integrality at cofinitely many places, matching [Stichtenoth Definition1.5.2](https://link.springer.com/chapter/10.1007/978-3-540-76878-4_1). Cofinite means a finite exceptional set, not a uniform valuation bound or eventuality along a chosen enumeration. The published exceptional-set equivalence and constant-one example check both interpretation and nonvacuity. Finite or empty place types are allowed, and zero entries automatically satisfy the valuation bound. [Lean source](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/93d1fe508e122e53ce5538a8a3994c290753f127/TauCeti/FieldTheory/FunctionField/Repartition/Basic.lean#L139).
The source identifies cofinite integrality with finiteness of the actual nonintegral exceptional set.
The published constant-one family is integral everywhere and belongs to the repartition space.

The exceptional set consists exactly of places where the entry has valuation greater than one. Its finiteness is equivalent to cofinite integrality, as required by [Stichtenoth Definition1.5.2](https://link.springer.com/chapter/10.1007/978-3-540-76878-4_1). This is not finiteness of the family’s support: infinitely many integral nonzero entries are allowed. The published constant-one and single-place formulas check both behaviors. Zero entries never enter the exceptional set, and no function-field finiteness assumption is used. [Lean source](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/93d1fe508e122e53ce5538a8a3994c290753f127/TauCeti/FieldTheory/FunctionField/Repartition/Basic.lean#L145).
The published constant-one family is integral everywhere and belongs to the repartition space.
The actual single-place repartition vanishes at every other place, including where divisor coefficients are negative.

The valuation-bound presentation is equivalent to actual membership in each local valuation ring at cofinitely many places. Thus Lean uses the same integrality condition as [Stichtenoth Definition1.5.2](https://link.springer.com/chapter/10.1007/978-3-540-76878-4_1), rather than residue-zero or unit membership. The source rewrites through the previously checked local-ring criterion. The constant-one family is a published control, and zero entries remain integral; no completeness or global function-field assumption enters. [Lean source](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/93d1fe508e122e53ce5538a8a3994c290753f127/TauCeti/FieldTheory/FunctionField/Repartition/Basic.lean#L150).
The actual valuation ring is exactly the subring cut out by valuation at most one.
The published constant-one family is integral everywhere and belongs to the repartition space.

Pointwise products remain integral away from the union of the two finite exceptional sets: multiplicativity gives v(ab)≤1 when both bounds hold. This verifies the ring closure noted in [Stichtenoth Definition1.5.2](https://link.springer.com/chapter/10.1007/978-3-540-76878-4_1). Neither factor must be nonzero or invertible. The published constant-one family and native single-place entries supply concrete carrier controls; the statement claims multiplication closure, not closure under arbitrary coordinatewise reciprocals. [Lean source](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/93d1fe508e122e53ce5538a8a3994c290753f127/TauCeti/FieldTheory/FunctionField/Repartition/Basic.lean#L161).
The published constant-one family is integral everywhere and belongs to the repartition space.
The actual single-place repartition has its prescribed entry at the selected place.

At each place the bound is v(a_P)≤exp(D_P), equivalent to order at least −D_P for nonzero entries. This is [Stichtenoth Definition1.5.3](https://link.springer.com/chapter/10.1007/978-3-540-76878-4_1), with zero handled correctly even when D_P<0. The published zero-divisor, guarded additive and single-place comparisons check the convention. The carrier is presented inside all F-valued families; its separate proved inclusion in the repartition space supplies the documented subspace interpretation. [Lean source](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/93d1fe508e122e53ce5538a8a3994c290753f127/TauCeti/FieldTheory/FunctionField/Repartition/Basic.lean#L172).
The source computes A_F(0) as the everywhere integral families, fixing the zero-divisor convention.
The source translates the multiplicative bound to order at each nonzero entry and explicitly handles zero entries separately.
The published native single-place family satisfies the divisor bound exactly when its selected entry does; all other entries are handled as zero in the source proof.

The displayed membership condition imposes the divisor bound at every place, not merely cofinitely many. Its sign agrees with [Stichtenoth Definition1.5.3](https://link.springer.com/chapter/10.1007/978-3-540-76878-4_1): poles are allowed up to D_P. The published zero-divisor formula and guarded additive comparison check that zero entries survive negative coefficients and that nonzero entries have order at least −D_P. The theorem asserts no dimension bound or exact-constants hypothesis. [Lean source](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/93d1fe508e122e53ce5538a8a3994c290753f127/TauCeti/FieldTheory/FunctionField/Repartition/Basic.lean#L188).
The source computes A_F(0) as the everywhere integral families, fixing the zero-divisor convention.
The source translates the multiplicative bound to order at each nonzero entry and explicitly handles zero entries separately.

Increasing a divisor relaxes every bound v(a_P)≤exp(D_P), so the subspace inclusion has the stated direction. This is the filtration monotonicity used in [Stichtenoth Theorem1.5.4, Step1](https://link.springer.com/chapter/10.1007/978-3-540-76878-4_1). The proof compares coefficients pointwise and exponentiation monotonically, without requiring effective divisors. Published zero-step and single-place formulas fix the sign and negative-coefficient behavior; no dimension or global Riemann–Roch conclusion is inferred. [Lean source](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/93d1fe508e122e53ce5538a8a3994c290753f127/TauCeti/FieldTheory/FunctionField/Repartition/Basic.lean#L211).
The source computes A_F(0) as the everywhere integral families, fixing the zero-divisor convention.
The published native single-place family satisfies the divisor bound exactly when its selected entry does; all other entries are handled as zero in the source proof.

The pointwise maximum of divisors corresponds to the sum of the two subspaces. The published proof explicitly splits each entry according to which bound it satisfies, giving both required summands; it does not assume a general subspace identity. This implements the repartition calculus of [Stichtenoth §I.5](https://link.springer.com/chapter/10.1007/978-3-540-76878-4_1). The actual single-place comparison and directedness theorem support the interpretation, including zero entries and incomparable divisors. [Lean source](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/93d1fe508e122e53ce5538a8a3994c290753f127/TauCeti/FieldTheory/FunctionField/Repartition/Basic.lean#L216).
The published native single-place family satisfies the divisor bound exactly when its selected entry does; all other entries are handled as zero in the source proof.
The published directedness witness is the pointwise maximum of the two divisors.

Outside the finite support of D, the defining bound reduces to v(a_P)≤1. Consequently every divisor-bounded family is a repartition, as intended by [Stichtenoth Definition1.5.3](https://link.springer.com/chapter/10.1007/978-3-540-76878-4_1). The source proves that the actual exceptional set lies in D.support, including negative coefficients and zero entries. The published finite-exception criterion and converse existence of a bound check that this is the intended filtration of A_F, without a finite-support condition on the family. [Lean source](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/93d1fe508e122e53ce5538a8a3994c290753f127/TauCeti/FieldTheory/FunctionField/Repartition/Basic.lean#L251).
The source identifies cofinite integrality with finiteness of the actual nonintegral exceptional set.
The source constructs a finite pole-bound divisor from the actual exceptional set, using max 0 of the negative orders and handling zero entries.

The source constructs a divisor on the finite nonintegral exceptional set, with coefficient max(0,−ord(a_P)); it proves that divisor bounds the family. Zero entries are handled separately, so ord(0)’s default value cannot invalidate the construction. This gives the exhaustion underlying [Stichtenoth’s repartition spaces](https://link.springer.com/chapter/10.1007/978-3-540-76878-4_1). The published literal-union identity records the result; the zero-divisor formula checks the everywhere-integral boundary. No uniform bound across infinitely many poles is assumed. [Lean source](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/93d1fe508e122e53ce5538a8a3994c290753f127/TauCeti/FieldTheory/FunctionField/Repartition/Basic.lean#L262).
The published set equality is the literal union of the actual divisor-bounded spaces; this is a structural consequence, not an independently constructed numerical example.
The source computes A_F(0) as the everywhere integral families, fixing the zero-divisor convention.

This is the range of the constant-family linear map, the diagonal object used in [Stichtenoth Definition1.5.2](https://link.springer.com/chapter/10.1007/978-3-540-76878-4_1). Published membership and constant-family formulas identify that range exactly. At an arbitrary extension with no places the range can collapse; the declaration itself does not assert injectivity. The separate inclusion into A_F retains IsFunctionField, where the usual diagonal embedding interpretation applies. No exact-constants or finite-dimensionality claim is hidden here. [Lean source](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/93d1fe508e122e53ce5538a8a3994c290753f127/TauCeti/FieldTheory/FunctionField/Repartition/Basic.lean#L305).
The actual range condition is equivalent to the family being constant, without claiming uniqueness when the place type is empty.
For an actual algebraic function field, the published finite-pole proof puts each constant family in the repartition space.

Diagonal membership means there exists one element f of F whose constant family is the given family. This is exactly the range formulation of the principal repartition in [Stichtenoth Definition1.5.2](https://link.springer.com/chapter/10.1007/978-3-540-76878-4_1). The statement uses existence, not uniqueness, so it remains correct if there are no places. Published constant-family membership and its L(D) comparison verify the intended interpretation. Cofinite integrality is a separate function-field theorem, not assumed by this equivalence. [Lean source](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/93d1fe508e122e53ce5538a8a3994c290753f127/TauCeti/FieldTheory/FunctionField/Repartition/Basic.lean#L311).
Every actual constant family is in the diagonal range; no function-field assumption is needed for this membership statement.
The published constant-family comparison is exactly membership in the native Riemann–Roch subspace, including the zero function.

The constant family with value f lies in the range defining the diagonal, witnessed by that very f. This is the principal-family construction in [Stichtenoth Definition1.5.2](https://link.springer.com/chapter/10.1007/978-3-540-76878-4_1), valid also for f=0 and an empty place type. The published range equivalence and constant-family L(D) comparison identify the object. The lemma does not assert that every constant family is cofinitely integral for an arbitrary extension; that needs the separate function-field hypothesis. [Lean source](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/93d1fe508e122e53ce5538a8a3994c290753f127/TauCeti/FieldTheory/FunctionField/Repartition/Basic.lean#L317).
The actual range condition is equivalent to the family being constant, without claiming uniqueness when the place type is empty.
The published constant-family comparison is exactly membership in the native Riemann–Roch subspace, including the zero function.

A function in an algebraic function field has only finitely many poles, so its constant family is integral cofinitely often. This is [Stichtenoth Corollary1.3.4 and Definition1.5.2](https://link.springer.com/chapter/10.1007/978-3-540-76878-4_1). Lean retains IsFunctionField and handles f=0 directly before converting a nonintegral valuation into nonzero order. The published finite-order-support theorem and constant-one case support the exact argument. Exact constants, finite base fields and separability are unnecessary for this conclusion. [Lean source](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/93d1fe508e122e53ce5538a8a3994c290753f127/TauCeti/FieldTheory/FunctionField/Repartition/Basic.lean#L322).
The published algebraic-function-field theorem proves finite support of the totalized order; the zero function is explicitly interpreted separately.
The published constant-one family is integral everywhere and belongs to the repartition space.

Every diagonal family has a constant representative f; the published finite-pole theorem places that family in A_F under the stated IsFunctionField hypothesis. This gives the subspace inclusion used in [Stichtenoth Definition1.5.2](https://link.springer.com/chapter/10.1007/978-3-540-76878-4_1). The native range and elementwise inclusion formulas check the actual maps. The statement is an inclusion, not a claim that all repartitions are diagonal or that the diagonal equals a divisor-bounded space. [Lean source](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/93d1fe508e122e53ce5538a8a3994c290753f127/TauCeti/FieldTheory/FunctionField/Repartition/Basic.lean#L336).
The actual range condition is equivalent to the family being constant, without claiming uniqueness when the place type is empty.
For an actual algebraic function field, the published finite-pole proof puts each constant family in the repartition space.

For a constant family, every coordinate bound is precisely the defining bound of the native L(D). Thus the equivalence identifies the diagonal filtration with [Stichtenoth’s Riemann–Roch space](https://link.springer.com/chapter/10.1007/978-3-540-76878-4_1), including the zero function and arbitrary negative divisor coefficients. The published intersection theorem states this as an equality of subspaces, and the zero-divisor formula checks integrality. No Riemann–Roch dimension formula, finite-dimensionality or exact-constants conclusion is asserted by this elementary comparison. [Lean source](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/93d1fe508e122e53ce5538a8a3994c290753f127/TauCeti/FieldTheory/FunctionField/Repartition/Basic.lean#L343).
The actual intersection with the diagonal is the image of L(D), rather than an asserted dimension or Riemann–Roch formula.
The source computes A_F(0) as the everywhere integral families, fixing the zero-divisor convention.

Lean takes the unit sphere in ℝⁿ⁺¹ modulo the integer units acting as identity and negation. This is exactly the antipodal-quotient model of real projective space in [Hatcher, Example0.4](https://pi.math.cornell.edu/~hatcher/AT/AT.pdf#page=15). The installed topology is the quotient topology, and `mk_eq_mk_iff` verifies that no additional points are identified. The published dimension-zero calculation gives one point. This carrier does not claim the separate smooth-atlas comparison with native Projectivization. [Source](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/93d1fe508e122e53ce5538a8a3994c290753f127/TauCeti/AlgebraicTopology/UniversalCover/RealProjective/Basic.lean#L58).
The quotient identifies exactly equal or antipodal unit representatives.
The installed topology makes the native projection a quotient map.

This is the actual projection sending a unit vector to its antipodal orbit, as in [Hatcher, Example0.4](https://pi.math.cornell.edu/~hatcher/AT/AT.pdf#page=15). Its domain is the sphere in EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin(n+1)); the abbreviated rendered sphere notation introduces no arbitrary ambient space. Published surjectivity and the equality criterion fix its range and fibres. It also works in dimension zero, where the two sphere points have the same image and the quotient has one point. [Source](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/93d1fe508e122e53ce5538a8a3994c290753f127/TauCeti/AlgebraicTopology/UniversalCover/RealProjective/Basic.lean#L83).
Every native projective point has a unit-vector preimage.
Antipodal vectors have equal image under this exact projection.

The statement says every point of the actual projective quotient has a unit-vector representative. This follows from the quotient carrier itself, matching the sphere description in [Hatcher, Example0.4](https://pi.math.cornell.edu/~hatcher/AT/AT.pdf#page=15); it does not assume a separately constructed bijection with lines. The source invokes quotient surjectivity directly, so no choice of normalization or distinguished representative enters the conclusion. The representative may be either antipode, and the assertion includes dimension zero. [Source](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/93d1fe508e122e53ce5538a8a3994c290753f127/TauCeti/AlgebraicTopology/UniversalCover/RealProjective/Basic.lean#L88).
The distinct-representative ambiguity is exactly antipodal equality.

Equality of these projective points means precisely that their unit representatives agree or are antipodal, as in [Hatcher, Example0.4](https://pi.math.cornell.edu/~hatcher/AT/AT.pdf#page=15). The proof unfolds orbit equality and uses that the only integer units are1 and−1; conversely those units witness each alternative. Restricting to the unit sphere is essential to this exact ± formulation. The two alternatives do not identify unrelated scalar multiples, and the statement remains valid for the two-point sphere in dimension zero. [Source](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/93d1fe508e122e53ce5538a8a3994c290753f127/TauCeti/AlgebraicTopology/UniversalCover/RealProjective/Basic.lean#L135).
The negative branch recovers the native antipodal-invariance formula.
Antipodal-invariant quotient elimination evaluates correctly on representatives.

The statement matches the antipodal covering-space action in [Hatcher, Proposition1.40 and Example1.43](https://pi.math.cornell.edu/~hatcher/AT/AT.pdf#page=81). Lean’s IsQuotientCoveringMap records the quotient topology, orbit fibres, and disjoint translates of suitable neighbourhoods. The source supplies a continuous free integer-unit action on the radius-one sphere; finiteness gives proper discontinuity. Consequently the fibres have two points. No simple-connectivity claim is made: the same covering statement correctly includes S¹→RP¹ and the disconnected S⁰→RP⁰ case. [Source](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/93d1fe508e122e53ce5538a8a3994c290753f127/TauCeti/AlgebraicTopology/UniversalCover/RealProjective/Basic.lean#L157).
The exact projection is an ordinary covering map.
Fibre equality is precisely equality or negation of unit vectors.

The projection equips the antipodal orbit set with the quotient topology used in [Hatcher, Example0.4](https://pi.math.cornell.edu/~hatcher/AT/AT.pdf#page=15). Lean’s IsQuotientMap includes surjectivity and the topology induced by inverse images; the proof obtains this exact property from the stronger quotient-cover theorem. It does not infer a homeomorphism from a bare orbit bijection. The assertion holds in every natural dimension, including the map from the discrete two-point sphere to RP⁰. [Source](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/93d1fe508e122e53ce5538a8a3994c290753f127/TauCeti/AlgebraicTopology/UniversalCover/RealProjective/Basic.lean#L165).
The exact quotient projection is continuous.
The stronger open-quotient statement confirms the same topology and map.

An antipodal-invariant function on the unit sphere descends uniquely to the orbit set defining RPⁿ in [Hatcher, Example0.4](https://pi.math.cornell.edu/~hatcher/AT/AT.pdf#page=15). Lean correctly allows any target Sort: this is set-theoretic quotient elimination, with no continuity promise. The proof checks both possible integer units, and the published `lift_mk` and `lift_unique` formulas establish evaluation and uniqueness. No representative is chosen, and invariance under negation suffices because the action has exactly those two elements. [Source](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/93d1fe508e122e53ce5538a8a3994c290753f127/TauCeti/AlgebraicTopology/UniversalCover/RealProjective/Basic.lean#L101).
Evaluation of the descended function on the native quotient map equals the original function.
Any function with the same representative values is this quotient lift.

This is the explicit upper-hemisphere coordinate construction underlying [Hatcher, Example0.4](https://pi.math.cornell.edu/~hatcher/AT/AT.pdf#page=15): retain v’s first k coordinates, append √(1−‖v‖²), and set later coordinates to zero. The docstring correctly restricts sphere membership to k≤n and ‖v‖≤1, and `norm_hemispherePoint` proves that case. The total formula remains meaningful outside this regime without asserting sphere membership. On the boundary the square-root coordinate vanishes, and the published negation formula verifies antipodal attaching behaviour. [Source](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/93d1fe508e122e53ce5538a8a3994c290753f127/TauCeti/Topology/CWComplex/Classical/RealProjective.lean#L68).
Under k≤n and ‖v‖≤1 the actual output has norm1.
On norm-one inputs the added coordinate vanishes and the construction commutes with negation.

Injectivity follows because all k input coordinates survive among the n+1 output coordinates. The precise bound is k≤n+1, appropriately weaker than the k≤n condition needed for an extra hemisphere coordinate. No unit-ball hypothesis is required for this coordinate assertion. When k=n+1 the formula retains every coordinate; when k=0 the domain is a singleton. This correctly supports the characteristic-map construction in [Hatcher, Example0.4](https://pi.math.cornell.edu/~hatcher/AT/AT.pdf#page=15). [Source](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/93d1fe508e122e53ce5538a8a3994c290753f127/TauCeti/Topology/CWComplex/Classical/RealProjective.lean#L124).
Each input coordinate is recovered verbatim at the corresponding output index.

The set consists of projective classes whose last nonzero coordinate is i: coordinate i is nonzero and all later coordinates vanish. This is the usual cell RPⁱ∖RPⁱ⁻¹ in [Hatcher, Example0.4](https://pi.math.cornell.edu/~hatcher/AT/AT.pdf#page=15). The representative criterion is invariant under negation, and the source proves distinct cells are disjoint. “Open cell” has its CW meaning here; the definition does not assert that a lower-dimensional cell is open in the whole projective space. [Source](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/93d1fe508e122e53ce5538a8a3994c290753f127/TauCeti/Topology/CWComplex/Classical/RealProjective.lean#L182).
Membership is exactly the coordinate criterion on any unit representative.
Different last-nonzero-coordinate strata are disjoint.

This criterion removes the existential representative from the open-cell definition: any chosen unit representative must have nonzero coordinate i and zero later coordinates. The equality-or-antipodes theorem justifies the reverse direction, since negation preserves both conditions. Thus the formula describes the coordinate stratum in [Hatcher, Example0.4](https://pi.math.cornell.edu/~hatcher/AT/AT.pdf#page=15) independently of representatives. It includes the zero-cell and imposes no unjustified positivity condition on coordinate i; positivity is only chosen later when constructing an inverse chart. [Source](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/93d1fe508e122e53ce5538a8a3994c290753f127/TauCeti/Topology/CWComplex/Classical/RealProjective.lean#L188).
The representative criterion yields disjointness of distinct coordinate cells.

The characteristic map implements [Hatcher, Example0.4](https://pi.math.cornell.edu/~hatcher/AT/AT.pdf#page=15) using the upper hemisphere and the antipodal quotient. A radial homeomorphism converts Mathlib’s sup-norm disk to the Euclidean disk, preserving its boundary. Its PartialEquiv source is the open ball and target the open cell; continuity is separately proved on the closed ball. The arbitrary value outside the closed ball is harmless because neither the characteristic-map assertion nor either inverse law uses that region. [Source](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/93d1fe508e122e53ce5538a8a3994c290753f127/TauCeti/Topology/CWComplex/Classical/RealProjective.lean#L262).
On the actual closed ball, the map is radial conversion followed by upper-hemisphere embedding and mk.
The closed-ball characteristic map is continuous, including its attaching boundary.
The inverse is continuous on the actual open cell.

The image of the open unit ball is exactly the coordinate-defined open cell, as required of the characteristic maps in [Hatcher, Example0.4](https://pi.math.cornell.edu/~hatcher/AT/AT.pdf#page=15). The source obtains equality from the proved PartialEquiv inverse laws, not from a dimension argument. This statement intentionally concerns the open ball: boundary points belong to lower-dimensional cells and need not map injectively. The zero-dimensional open ball is a singleton, giving the correct zero-cell case. [Source](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/93d1fe508e122e53ce5538a8a3994c290753f127/TauCeti/Topology/CWComplex/Classical/RealProjective.lean#L356).
The PartialEquiv source is precisely the open unit ball.
The PartialEquiv target is precisely the stated open cell.

The characteristic map is continuous on the entire closed unit ball, including its attaching boundary. The proof uses the source’s exact closed-ball formula: radial change of norm, continuous upper-hemisphere embedding, and the continuous quotient projection.
